key_insight: CAHR reconstructs detector error models as discrete hypergraphs from syndrome statistics with a globally consistent, false-positive-free pruning strategy, enabling more faithful circuit-level noise inference.
engineering_relevance: This matters for quantum hardware and decoder design because accurate multi-body error characterization can improve fault-tolerant decoding and noise-model calibration in real devices.
method: Use exact algebraic correlation equations to infer candidate error mechanisms from observed syndromes.
Apply a top-down concurrent-pruning strategy to remove inconsistent mechanisms while preserving true correlations.
Separate topology recovery from probability fitting, especially in dense codes where variance cascades hinder direct continuous estimation.
evidence_signal: In benchmark tests on d=5 rotated surface codes and dense 8-body 2D color codes, the method recovered fault topology without false positives.
watch_item: The paper notes that exact continuous parameter extraction can be limited by variance cascade, so topology recovery and probability optimization may need to be done in two stages.
paper_title: Reconstruction of detector error model for quantum error correction
